item.description:
Seshctl 0.8.1

Repo colors no longer clash

With repo color coding on, two repos could end up with the same color. Each repo’s color was picked without looking at the others, so with five or six repos a clash was more likely than not. Now a repo that would clash gets the free color that looks most different, and keeps it from then on. Searching History doesn’t use up colors.

You’ll see a one-time change: some repos that shared a color get a new one.

Repo names as chips

In the compact layout, the repo name at the right of each row is now a soft tinted chip in the repo’s color, instead of monospaced text. Tree view group headers use a larger version of the same chip, and section headers like Today and Yesterday no longer use a monospaced font.

Fixes

  • The cyan repo color is dimmer, so it no longer stands out from the rest.

Seshctl 0.8.0

Search your whole history

Typing in the panel now also searches every message from every past session, not just the rows on screen. Matches show up in a History section, one row per session, with the matched words highlighted. Each word you type matches as a prefix, and "quoted text" matches a phrase. Sessions whose title matches rank first.

Claude Code deletes transcripts after 30 days, but Seshctl keeps the text. Those rows are marked transcript deleted, and Enter shows the conversation rebuilt from search history instead of trying to resume it.

Retitle a session with t

Claude Code titles a session once, from its first prompt, so a long session keeps the name of its first task. Press t to have Claude suggest a title for what the session is doing now. y keeps it, n or Esc declines it. It needs the claude CLI installed.

See each session’s model

Rows show a small pill with the session’s model, like “Opus 5.5” or “GPT-5.6 Terra”. It turns amber when a session isn’t on the model you usually use for that agent.

Codex rows get titles

Codex sessions now show their thread names as row titles, instead of falling back to the branch or folder.

Sessions in the Claude app’s Code tab

Enter on a session you started in the Claude desktop app’s Code tab now opens that session in the app, instead of just bringing the app forward. It also reopens sessions that have finished.

Fixes

  • Agent badges use the real Codex mark and Claude’s brand color.
  • VoiceOver reads rows as “Ghostty, Claude Code”.

Thanks to @patoms for the model pill and agent naming work in this release.

Seshctl 0.7.0

Reopen closed sessions with c

Press c to swap the list for your closed sessions, one row per conversation, newest first. Enter resumes the selected one in a new tab, and / searches within it. Esc or q goes back to the live list. Press it again to close the panel.

Search matches every word

Search now matches each word you type separately, across the title, repo, branch, folder and messages. sesh dedupe finds a seshctl session about deduplication even though the two words live in different fields.

Pin the panel open

Settings → Appearance → Keep panel open turns the panel into a dashboard you can park on a spare monitor. It stays put, remembers its size and position, and dims when you’re not using it. Always in front keeps it above other windows. While it’s pinned, Seshctl appears in the Dock and Cmd+Tab. Otherwise it stays a menu-bar app.

Rows stay still while you’re using the panel

Rows used to jump to the top whenever a session updated, which could move the row you were about to click. The order now freezes while the panel is open. A pinned panel re-sorts only when you’re not hovering over it or using it.

Remote sessions open in the Claude app

If the Claude desktop app is installed, Enter on a remote row (and w on a bridged one) opens the session there instead of a browser tab. Remote rows show the Claude app icon.

Fixes

  • x ends rows whose process is already gone. Codex rows could get stuck as active after their process died.
  • Codex:
    • Seshctl registers the SessionEnd hook, so Codex rows end when the session does.
    • Resume uses codex resume.
    • The prompt hook passes Codex’s matcher validation.
  • Ghostty focuses the exact split pane on builds that support it.
  • Upgrades no longer let the hook guard uninstall Seshctl mid-upgrade.
  • New app icon and menu bar glyph.
  • Repo colors:
    • More distinct across repos.
    • Moved off GitHub’s merged-purple and open-green.

Thanks to @patoms for a big batch of contributions to this release.
